transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry

tell me your dream, however it comes back to you. bits and pieces are fine

hey berry
ok so the part i keep thinking about is there was this fish, a silver one, and it said my name. like looked right at me and said it. nobody else heard it
it was at a night market, i was there with my older sister

oh, a fish saying your name. and only you heard it

what was it like when it said it?

honestly i don't remember what it sounded like, it just said it
it was lying on ice at this old man's stall, my sister wanted to buy fish. and then he wrapped it in newspaper and gave it to me, and i held it against my chest

that's okay, it just said it. that's how dreams do it

and then you were holding it against your chest, wrapped in newspaper

what was that like, holding it there?

i don't really remember how it felt, i just held it
after that we were on one bike, my sister pedalling and me on the back with the fish, going over this narrow iron bridge. and it started raining

the two of you on one bike, you on the back with the fish, and then the rain

what was the bridge like?

it was narrow and iron, over a river that was totally black. i don't remember much else about it
the rain was big warm drops, and the market lights were behind us by then

big warm drops, the black river underneath, and the market lights behind you

when you picture yourself on the back of that bike, are you seeing it through your own eyes, or more like watching the two of you from somewhere outside?

hmm i don't really remember, i can't say either way
but then the fish said my name again, quietly, and that's when i woke up

it said your name again, quietly, and then you woke up

besides the fish, was there anything else there that mattered to you, or was it really just the fish?

mostly the fish honestly. but my sister being there too i guess, she was the one who wanted fish in the first place. and there were these strings of little yellow lights over all the stalls, and it was super crowded, like hundreds of people. that's about all i've got

hundreds of people under all those little yellow lights, and your sister the one who wanted fish

do you remember how it started? like the first thing, were you already at the market with her?
yeah i think we were just already there, in the crowd with all the lights. i don't remember getting there or anything before that

just already there in the crowd with all the lights, that's so often how dreams start

i think i've got a good feel for it now. anything else come back to you, or is that the dream?
oh one thing, the fish was pretty big, about as long as my arm. but yeah other than that i think that's the whole dream

as long as your arm, that's a big fish to hold against your chest

ok so here's your dream. you and your older sister are already at a night market, super crowded, hundreds of people, strings of little yellow lights over all the stalls. she wants to buy fish. at an old man's stall there's a silver fish lying on ice, about as long as your arm, and it looks right at you and says your name. nobody else hears it. the old man wraps it in newspaper and gives it to you, and you hold it against your chest. then you're on one bike, your sister pedalling, you on the back with the fish, going over a narrow iron bridge above a river that's totally black. the market lights are behind you now and it starts raining, big warm drops. the fish says your name again, quietly, and you wake up

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
yeah that's it, you got it all right. nothing missing that i can think of

good, i'm glad i've got it

would you like to see it drawn?
yeah, i'd like that

okay, here are a few ways it could look. watercolour on rough paper, warm and hushed, like a memory the rain has half washed. or an old woodcut print, quiet and a little solemn, like a folk tale that already knows how it ends. or a soft pencil drawing, gentle and fragile, like something you could lose if you looked away. or a photo, real and close, like you were really there on that crowded, rainy night

which one feels closest? or you can tell me your own way
the photo i think. it felt pretty real, like i was actually there

a photo then, like you were really there

i'll start with the old man who runs the fish stall. i picture him as just an old man, and my guess is he's got a plain apron on over his everyday clothes

anything different from how you saw him, or would you leave him to me?
yeah he was just an old man, i don't remember what he was wearing. go with your guess, the apron sounds fine

okay, i'm sketching the old man, the fish, your sister, the night market, the iron bridge, the bike and the newspaper now. they'll show up on the right

you're in it too, so i'll draw you as well. do you want to be drawn as you are, and tell me a little about yourself, or should i just imagine you?
you can just imagine me, that's fine. i don't really remember what i looked like in the dream anyway

that's fine, i'll imagine you

i'm sketching you now, and everything's being sketched together. it'll all show up on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks wrong once it's there, just tell me
ok cool, i see them. they look right to me

good, i'm glad

so looking at all of it there, the fish and your sister and the old man, the crowd, the bridge and the bike, does it look the way you remember it?
yeah it looks right, pretty much how i remember it. kind of weird seeing the fish like that actually

yeah, it's a strange thing to see a fish from a dream just sitting there looking back at you

okay, everything's sketched now. next i'll draw the moments of your dream in order, each one carrying on from the ones before it, and they'll show up on the right as they're ready
ok cool, i see the first one. looks right so far, i'll wait for the rest

good, you and your sister at the start, in the crowd

the next ones are on their way now, they'll pop up on the right one after another
ok, still just the one there. i'll keep an eye out for the others
yeah, the others are still being drawn. they'll show up on the right soon, one after another
oh the second one's up now. looks right to me

the fish on the ice, looking right at you. glad that's how you saw it

the other four carry on from that moment, so i'm drawing them now. they'll show up on the right one after another
ok cool, i'll wait for the rest. no rush
okay, the other four are still coming. they'll show up on the right soon
the third one's up now, looks right to me too

the old man handing you the fish in newspaper. glad that one's right too

the last three carry on from that moment, so i'm drawing them now. they'll show up on the right one after another
ok cool, i'll wait for the last three
okay, the last three are on their way. they'll show up on the right soon
the fourth one's there now, looks right. two more to go

you holding the fish against your chest, wrapped in newspaper. glad that one's right

the last two carry on from there, so i'm drawing them now. they'll show up on the right soon
ok, i'll wait for the last two
okay, the last two are still being drawn. they'll show up on the right soon
fifth one's up, looks right. just the last one left

your sister pedalling over that narrow iron bridge, you on the back with the fish. glad it looks right

the last one carries on from there, so i'm drawing it now. it'll show up on the right soon
ok, i'll wait for the last one
okay, the last one's still being drawn. it'll show up on the right soon
oh the last one's up now. looks right to me, that's pretty much how it ended

the two of you on the bike in the warm rain, and the fish saying your name one last time

now that all six are there together, does it look the way you remember it?
yeah, all six together look right. that's pretty much the dream, start to finish. kinda strange seeing it all laid out like that, thanks

yeah, it's a strange thing, seeing a dream laid out start to finish like that

thank you for sharing it with me. the fish, your sister, the warm rain on the bridge. all six are there on the right, in order, whenever you want to look back through it
